newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BANKS MUST MARK-TO-MKT PORTFOLIOS BY DEC 31 - BOG.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BANKS MUST MARK-TO-MKT PORTFOLIOS BY DEC 31 - BOG.

text.p: Greek credit institutions will have to mark-to-market their portfolios effective December 31, 1996 in compliance with a central bank decree that clarifies regulations of law 2396/96 that harmonises Greek legislation with the European Union.
The decree also sets uniform rules for the calculation of capital requirements for market risk linking all risks assumed by credit institutions to their equity capital, it said in a statement.
The capital adequacy requirements for market risk are added to the existing ones for credit risk and the minimum total capital adequacy ratio cannot be less than 8.0 percent, it said.

The decree also clarifies the methodology of measuring positions of portfolio trades for asset and liability items and off-balance sheet items whose share to traditional bank products and services rises to facilitate monitoring by banks and the Bank of Greece.

The meaning of portfolio trades is defined and distinguished from the investment portfolio. New capital adequacy requirements for trades are imposed in connection with market risks such as positions in debited bonds and stocks and transaction risk from trades in derivatives and open forex positions.

The specialised processes for monitoring market risks go into effect on December 31, 1996 and affect all credit institutions based in Greece, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
